title: Smear, culture, and what each proves
dek: Smear is density and infection-control speed. Culture is viability and the substrate for phenotypic DST. Neither is a complete DST panel.
story: Acid-fast smear (Ziehl–Neelsen or auramine fluorochrome) answers: are there acid-fast bodies in this specimen, and roughly how many (IUATLD/WHO 0 to 3+)? It is fast, cheap, and a transmission-risk proxy. It does not name MTBC versus NTM, does not prove viability, and does not grade rifampin.

Culture remains the microbiologic reference for viability. Liquid MGIT grows faster than Löwenstein–Jensen; time-to-positivity is a crude burden biomarker. Contamination is data. A negative culture after a blazing Xpert can be dead bacilli, prior treatment, or a lab problem — write the differential, do not ignore it.

Phenotypic DST is performed on cultured growth (or, in some protocols, direct). It is still required as a residual against catalogues, and it is the only path when the genome is silent. It is slow, critical-concentration-dependent, and not the first test WHO wants you to wait for before treating.
deepTitle: How to not over-read the bottle
deep: Fluorochrome smear is more sensitive than ZN in most programmes; confirmation practice varies. Smear-negative never meant “not infectious,” only “less so.”
MGIT TTP of 3 days versus 18 days is a different N. Do not average them in a paper without a model.
Mixed NTM+Mtb cultures happen. A bottle that “looks AFB positive” after a negative NAAT is an NTM until speciation.
Storage, decontamination (NaOH), and transport kill bacilli. Pediatric gastric aspirates are a race against neutrophil and acid.

visual.caption: Smear for speed and density; culture for viability and pDST; speciation whenever the bottle and the NAAT disagree.

example.title: Xpert high, culture negative
example.setup: Retreatment patient, Ultra “MTB high, RIF not detected,” smear scanty, MGIT negative at 42 days.

steps.title: DNA is not CFU
steps.body: High NAAT can be leftover nucleic acid, especially after recent treatment, or a culture kill during decontamination.

steps.title: Repeat a specimen, not a superstition
steps.body: New sputum, consider non-sputum sites, check decontamination logs.

steps.title: Do not write RIF-S as a phenotype
steps.body: You have a NAAT RIF window on possibly dead bacilli. Clinical disease status is a different question.

choices: High density of acid-fast bodies and, in pulmonary specimens, higher transmission risk
check.answer: High density of acid-fast bodies and, in pulmonary specimens, higher transmission risk
check.why: Smear is not speciation and not DST.

check.prompt: MGIT flags positive at day 4 versus day 20, same specimen type. The day-4 bottle is best read as:
choices: Higher viable burden (shorter TTP), all else equal
check.answer: Higher viable burden (shorter TTP), all else equal
check.why: Time-to-positivity is a crude N estimator, confounded by decontamination and mix.

whyWrong.Lower burden: Longer TTP is the low-burden pattern.
